To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of activity and the exploratory activity are independent of the sequential response organization.
the three measures of motor activity (counts, alpha, h) are independent and that the amount of exploratory activity is a separate factor.

unconditioned behavior of rats can be described by three independent factors: the amount of activity (counts), the sequential structure of the behavior (h) and the exploratory activity (rearings and holepokes).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a new approach to the quantitative description of behavior.
the description of the behavioral organization of unconditionized behavior in terms of its geometrical structure, temporal scaling, sequential response organization, and exploratory activity.
the development and application of a new approach for the analysis of unconditioned animal behavior, the temporal and spatial scaling approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amount of activity is a separate factor from the sequential and geometrical structure of motor activity.
the amount of motor behavior is influenced by three independent factors.

the three independent factors, i.e. amount of activity, sequential response organization, and exploratory behavior, can be used to describe the behavioral organization of rats in an unconditioned environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amount of unconditioned activity is not a simple function of the sequential or the geometrical characteristics of the behavior.
the amount of activity (counts), sequential response organization (h) and exploratory activity (rearings) are independent factors that characterize unconditioned rat motor activity.
the amount, sequential and geometric characteristics of motor activity can be assessed independently and are useful to study the neural mechanisms involved in the generation of behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of activity and the spatial scaling exponent can be used to describe the behavior in an independent manner.
the amount, the sequential structure and the geometrical structure are three independent factors that influence the motor activity in rats.
a combination of different measures of behavior can be used to characterize and describe the behavioral phenotype of an animal in a more complete and robust way.
